newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain stalls Manitoba harvest at 75 pct complete.
newsitem.headline: Rain stalls Manitoba harvest at 75 pct complete.

text.p: Manitoba's harvest stalled at last week's level of 75 percent complete on up to two inches of rain late last week, Manitoba Agriculture's report for the week ended September 30 said.

Southwest Manitoba - Eighty percent of crops were combined with yields seen at or above average. Harvest progress was slow with poor drying conditions impeding combining until late last week. Sunday morning saw lows of -4.0 Celsius with damage seen minimal because of the advanced stage of the crop.
Northwest Manitoba - Sixty percent of crops were combined with yields above average, 95 percent of crops were swathed.
Five to 15 mm of rain virtually stopped harvest progress. The first widespread killing frost struck the region on the weekend.
Central Manitoba - Seventy-five percent of cereals were combined and 50 percent of oilseeds were combined. Rain Thursday and Friday stopped the harvest. Frost struck the region two nights.

Eastern Manitoba - Cereals were 75 to 90 percent combined, 50 percent of canola was harvested. Rainfall ranged from 1.0 to 2.0 inches and halted harvest progress. There has not yet been a general killing frost.

Interlake region - Eighty percent of cereals, 75 percent of canola and 50 percent of flax were combined. Yields were above average. Rainfall of up to 0.5 inch delayed harvest progress. A frost of -3.0 Celsius was reported across the region on the weekend.
